detail.longDescription: I need to update a jsonb column of a specific row in database. It holds a JSON object with session_id : group_key . On insert some key:value pairs will be added, then I need to add a new session_id to this JSON. It should be one atomic update operation and I don't need to select the current state of the row first before updating and writing it. I have already written the code that works, but I'm trying to make sure it's really atomic and efficient. First solution: async def add_group_member_session_group_key( session: AsyncSession, group_id: int, user_id: int, user_session_id: uuid.UUID, session_group_key: tuple ): query = ( update(GroupChatMember) .where( GroupChatMember.group_id==group_id, GroupChatMember.user_id==user_id, ) .values( group_key=GroupChatMember.group_key.op("||")( cast( {str(user_session_id): session_group_key}, JSONB, ) ) ) ) await session.execute(query) await session.commit() Second solution: async def add_group_member_session_group_key( session: AsyncSession, group_id: int, user_id: int, user_session_id: uuid.UUID, session_group_key: tuple ): query = ( update(GroupChatMember) .where( GroupChatMember.group_id==group_id, GroupChatMember.user_id==user_id, ) .values( group_key=GroupChatMember.group_key + literal( {user_session_id: session_group_key}, JSONB ) ) ) await session.execute(query) await session.commit() Is there any difference between these in terms of efficiency or atomicity?
